title: Tart Cranberry Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Sieved, sweetened cranberry purée whisked into a four-yolk custard.
summary: A sieved, sweetened cranberry purée whisked into a lighter version of our classic custard. Sharp, fruity and a cheerful pink.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the cranberries
steps.text: Simmer the cranberries with the water and 70 g sugar in the small pan for 8-10 min until they burst and collapse. Push through the sieve to remove the skins, then chill the purée; cranberries are rich in pectin, which gives the ice cream body.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Heat the cream, milk and salt until steaming. Whisk the yolks with 100 g sugar, whisk in two ladles of the hot dairy and return to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir steadily over low heat to 77-80 °C, until the custard coats the back of the spatula. Watch the temperature closely; it should not bubble.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain it, add the vanilla, then cool quickly in the iced water bath and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Whisk in the cold cranberry purée and churn until thick and creamy.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 4 h before serving.

tips: Frozen cranberries work straight from the freezer; add 2 min to the cooking time.
A common mistake is cutting the sugar too far; cranberries are very tart and need it.
Grated orange zest in the purée is a nice addition.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
